card.name: Subject before a past-tense or hypothetical verb
card.fires_on: A subject word (he, they, it, you, electron) right after a clause opener like if, wished, when, or status, where a past-tense or conditional verb such as had, was, were or could comes next.

modes.label: After if / wish / if only
modes.description: Subject pronoun in a hypothetical or wished-for clause, followed by could or were.
modes.example: Berkley said he wished<< he>> could take some parents in the developed world

modes.label: Past-time relative clause
modes.description: Subject in a clause about an earlier state, followed by had.
modes.example: This is an improvement on a few years ago when<< they>> had to rely on trucks to bring it

card.writes: It lowers was, were and similar verbs and raises could, suggesting the next word is a modal or had-type verb.
card.plain: It marks a subject word that is about to be followed by a past or hypothetical verb like had or could.
